content.text:
I've submitted index 3 (Sb fraction 0.353) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of the five I measured, at 0.073%.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.280 | 0.043 |
| **3** | **0.353** | **0.073** |
| 4 | 0.383 | 0.055 |
| 8 | 0.513 | 0.018 |
| 13 | 0.659 | 0.0005 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is highest around Sb ≈ 0.35 and drops on both sides. Compositions with more antimony, including the PbSb₂O₆ region near 0.66, perform poorly.
- **Structure:** index 3's XRD matches the Pb₂Sb₂O₇ pyrochlore best, with a similarity of 0.76. It probably also contains a second, lead-rich phase.
- **Still uncertain:** I didn't measure indices 1, 2 or 5–7, so one of them could beat index 3 slightly. The Sb-rich end (0.82 and above) was also never measured for EQE. I ruled it out because EQE kept falling as Sb went up and its XRD pattern differs from index 3's.
- **How I picked the last point:** the built-in GP suggestion wasn't useful because it just pointed to the unexplored Sb-rich end. Instead I fitted a parabola through the first three points, which put the peak near 0.38. Index 4 at 0.383 came in below index 3, so the true peak is probably just under 0.38.

All 5 EQE measurements are used. I used 2 of the 5 XRD measurements, on indices 3 and 20.
